resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Certificate of Compliance for Sale Application (on the City's Get a Permit or License page, Inspections Division forms) and schedule an inspection before closing. Submit it to the Division of Inspections, 515 Watchung Avenue. The application asks about the property, legal occupancy, buyer, closing date, permits and smoke/CO detectors. An LLC applicant must also give its Certificate of Formation. To close on a temporary certificate, the buyer signs a notarized affidavit and $500 per unit escrow is posted by certified check or money order.

resale_co.notes: Plainfield requires a Certificate of Compliance before the sale, transfer, rent or lease of property (Municipal Code Section 6:5-2). The City's FAQ page quotes the June 2026 sale application fees; the sale application linked on the forms page is dated December 2022 and shows the same residential fees ($50.00 first unit, $25.00 each additional). A temporary Certificate of Compliance may be approved in some sales when the property is in substantial compliance (buyer's notarized affidavit, $500 per unit escrow, life-safety items fixed first). Exemptions (for example a Certificate of Occupancy issued within 90 days, a refinance with no change in ownership) need an exemption application and the $75 fee. The 2022 form names Division of Inspections Director Leticia Velez (leticia.velez@plainfieldnj.gov, 908-753-3386); the current page lists Athenee Wright for general assistance. Rentals need their own Certificate of Compliance for Rental; that is a rental requirement.

requirements: Smoke alarm on each level including basements (not attics unless finished, or crawl spaces)
Smoke alarm and carbon monoxide alarm near any flame-producing device, outside each sleeping area and within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery type; combination smoke/CO 10-year sealed alarms are acceptable
Homes with a low-voltage alarm system need an alarm test report from a NJ certified fire protection contractor

Portable fire extinguisher (2A:10BC, no more than 10 pounds) in the kitchen, no more than 5 feet above the floor, new with receipt or serviced and tagged within 12 months (2021 form; the City payment notice still names the extinguisher certificate)
Only one- and two-family dwellings are inspected; inspections are on Wednesdays

authorities.how_to_apply: Pay online through the City's 'Smoke Home Inspections' GovPayNow page (card or e-check; a processing fee applies) or fill out the Application for Inspection Certification of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance and e-mail it to fireinspection@plainfieldnj.gov. Then call (908) 753-3446 to confirm payment; the bureau e-mails the inspection date. By mail or in person, checks are payable to Plainfield Fire Department (personal checks only for the $45.00 fee).

fire_cert.notes: Fees are from the City's current GovPayNow 'smoke home inspections' page (linked from the City fire page and the City's 2023 payment notice), which adds two-family and reinspection amounts. The City's application form (revised December 2021) lists the one-family amounts ($45.00 / $90.00 / $161.00) and still requires a portable fire extinguisher; state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed the extinguisher from the sale certificate in February 2025, so confirm with the bureau. The 2021 form names Fire Official Taheem Muslim; the state directory (July 2026) lists Anthony Pineda (anthony.pineda@plainfieldnj.gov) as Fire Official, so Pineda is used. The Fire Department contact page also lists fire.prevention@plainfieldnj.gov.
